question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
sql:
WITH daily_balances AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        CAST(txn_date AS DATE) as txn_date,
        CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END as balance_change,
        SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) 
            OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY CAST(txn_date AS DATE)) as running_balance
    FROM customer_transactions
),
rolling_avg AS (
    SELECT 
        a.customer_id,
        a.txn_date,
        a.running_balance,
        AVG(b.running_balance) as rolling_30day_avg
    FROM daily_balances a
    LEFT JOIN daily_balances b 
        ON a.customer_id = b.customer_id
        AND b.txn_date <= a.txn_date
        AND b.txn_date > a.txn_date - INTERVAL '30' DAY
    GROUP BY a.customer_id, a.txn_date, a.running_balance
),
customer_first_date AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        MIN(CAST(txn_date AS DATE)) as first_date
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_first_month AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', MIN(CAST(txn_date AS DATE))) as first_month
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
rolling_avg_with_month AS (
    SELECT 
        r.customer_id,
        r.txn_date,
        GREATEST(COALESCE(r.rolling_30day_avg, 0), 0) as rolling_30day_avg_clamped,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', r.txn_date) as txn_month,
        cf.first_month
    FROM rolling_avg r
    JOIN customer_first_date fd ON r.customer_id = fd.customer_id
    JOIN customer_first_month cf ON r.customer_id = cf.customer_id
    WHERE (r.txn_date - fd.first_date) >= 30
),
monthly_max AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        txn_month,
        MAX(rolling_30day_avg_clamped) as max_30day_avg
    FROM rolling_avg_with_month
    WHERE txn_month > first_month
    GROUP BY customer_id, txn_month
),
monthly_sum AS (
    SELECT 
        txn_month,
        SUM(max_30day_avg) as total_max_30day_avg
    FROM monthly_max
    GROUP BY txn_month
    ORDER BY txn_month
)
SELECT txn_month, ROUND(total_max_30day_avg, 2) as total_max_30day_avg
FROM monthly_sum

    FROM customer_transactions

rolling_avg AS (
    SELECT

        a.txn_date,
        a.running_balance,
        AVG(b.running_balance) as rolling_30day_avg
    FROM daily_balances a
    LEFT JOIN daily_balances b 
        ON a.customer_id = b.customer_id
        AND b.txn_date <= a.txn_date
        AND b.txn_date > a.txn_date - INTERVAL '30' DAY
    GROUP BY a.customer_id, a.txn_date, a.running_balance
),
customer_first_date AS (

        MIN(CAST(txn_date AS DATE)) as first_date

    GROUP BY customer_id

    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
rolling_avg_with_month AS (
    SELECT 
        r.customer_id,
        r.txn_date,
        GREATEST(COALESCE(r.rolling_30day_avg, 0), 0) as rolling_30day_avg_clamped,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', r.txn_date) as txn_month,
        cf.first_month

),

        txn_month,
        MAX(rolling_30day_avg_clamped) as max_30day_avg

    GROUP BY customer_id, txn_month
),
monthly_sum AS (
    SELECT 
        txn_month,
        SUM(max_30day_avg) as total_max_30day_avg
